chain.label: ILS runway 06/24 closed; only the short nonprecision runway 18 available at arrival
chain.trigger: A NOTAM in effect at the time of the accident indicated that runway 06/24, the longest runway available at the airport and the one with a precision approach, would be closed from 0400 to 0500 CDT.

chain.label: dark night approach at 0447 local time
chain.trigger: dark night visual flight rules conditions prevailed at the airport

chain.label: variable low ceiling over the approach course; actual cloud base about 350 ft above field elevation
chain.trigger: variable instrument meteorological conditions with a variable ceiling were present north of the airport on the approach course at the time of the accident

chain.label: wooded rising and downsloping terrain north of the runway 18 threshold
chain.trigger: The PAPI for runway 18 was set to project a glidepath of 3.2° to accommodate the rising terrain off the approach end of the runway.

chain.label: first officer fatigued from acute sleep loss; both pilots operating in the window of circadian low
chain.trigger: the first officer's fatigue due to acute sleep loss resulting from her ineffective off-duty time management and circadian factors

chain.label: captain's repeated training deficiencies on nonprecision/vertical-speed approaches; crews rarely fly nonprecision approaches in line operations
chain.trigger: the captain's training records revealed multiple substandard elements related to nonprecision approaches (most recently June 2013)

chain.label: dispatcher did not brief the crew on the runway closure, the single-approach option, or the 0500 reopening
chain.trigger: the dispatcher did not discuss the low ceilings, the single-approach option to the airport, or the reopening of runway 06/24 about 0500 with the flight crew

caused_by.evidence: Because the flight's scheduled arrival time was 0451, only the shorter runway 18 with a nonprecision approach was available to the crew.

chain.label: METAR remarks reporting a variable 600-1,300 ft ceiling stripped from the UPS weather feed and omitted from ATIS
chain.trigger: the meteorological aerodrome reports provided to the crew did not contain information about variable ceilings at BHM because the weather dissemination system used by UPS automatically removed the 'remarks' section of METAR reports

chain.label: flight plan never verified or sequenced in the FMC; direct-to-KBHM leg and discontinuity left active
chain.trigger: the captain did not request and the first officer did not verify that the flight plan reflected only the approach fixes; therefore, the direct-to-KBHM leg that had been set up during the flight from Louisville remained in the FMC

caused_by.evidence: the crew was engaged in a conversation about the lack of approach options to the runway and their perception that ATC had left them high on the approach... their conversation regarding nonpertinent operational issues distracted them from recognizing that the FMC was not resequenced even though several salient cues were available

the first officer did not clear the route discontinuity in the FMC (something that should be almost automatic, as it is done on every UPS flight)... fatigue likely further negatively affected the first officer's performance

chain.label: profile mode could not engage and the FMC computed a meaningless glidepath that pegged the VDI full-scale up
chain.trigger: This caused a flight plan discontinuity message to remain in the FMC, which rendered the glideslope generated for the profile approach meaningless.

caused_by.evidence: because the flight crew did not verify that the flight plan was sequenced, the autopilot could not engage in profile mode

chain.label: captain switched the autopilot to vertical speed mode without rebriefing the first officer
chain.trigger: When the autopilot did not engage in profile mode, the captain changed the autopilot mode to the vertical speed mode, yet he did not brief the first officer of the autopilot mode change.

caused_by.evidence: the captain likely perceived that the autopilot did not capture the profile glidepath and chose to change the autopilot from profile mode to vertical speed mode to manually command a descent

chain.label: 1,500 fpm descent commanded and held through the charted glidepath and through 1,000 ft above field elevation
chain.trigger: The captain then increased the vertical descent rate to 1,500 fpm, and the airplane continued to descend at that rate as it approached the IMTOY stepdown fix.

caused_by.evidence: by selecting the vertical speed mode, the approach essentially became a 'dive and drive' approach

getting behind on a localizer approach using vertical speed, descending to an incorrect altitude on a nonprecision approach using vertical speed... Most of these errors were associated with flying a nonprecision approach.

chain.label: neither pilot monitored altitude after the 1,000-ft callout; required minimums callouts omitted while both looked outside for the runway
chain.trigger: the first officer did not make the required callouts regarding approaching and reaching the minimum descent altitude, and the captain did not arrest the descent at the minimum descent altitude

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew's expectation that they would break out of the clouds at 1,000 feet above ground level due to incomplete weather information
they only saw the runway about 5 seconds before impacting the trees
dark night visual flight rules conditions prevailed at the airport
with the time compression resulting from the excessive descent rate and her fatigued state, it proved catastrophic
Because the captain did not communicate his intentions, it was not possible for the first officer to have a shared understanding of the approach, and her situational awareness was degraded.
The airplane reached these altitudes far faster than the first officer would have expected because of the excessive descent rate.

chain.label: airplane descended below the 1,200 ft minimum descent altitude to about 250 ft agl on a trajectory 1 nm short of the runway
chain.trigger: an inadvertent descent below the minimum approach altitude and subsequently into terrain

caused_by.evidence: the airplane continued to descend at 1,500 fpm and passed through and continued below the desired glidepath

the flight crew did not sufficiently monitor the airplane's altitude during the approach and subsequently allowed the airplane to descend below the minimum altitude without having the runway environment in sight

chain.label: unstabilized approach continued rather than a go-around, including after the EGPWS 'sink rate' caution alert
chain.trigger: the flight crew's continuation of an unstabilized approach

caused_by.evidence: Once the airplane descended below 1,000 ft at a descent rate greater than 1,000 fpm, the approach would have violated the stabilized approach criteria defined in the UPS flight operations manual and would have required a go-around.
The captain began to adjust the vertical speed in accordance with UPS's trained procedure... the airplane continued to descend at a rate of about 1,000 fpm
the captain's poor performance during the accident flight was consistent with past performance deficiencies in flying nonprecision approaches noted during training

chain.label: airplane struck trees, power lines, and terrain about 1.2 mi short of runway 18 and was destroyed by impact and fire
chain.trigger: crashed short of runway 18 during a localizer nonprecision approach to runway 18 at Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was still descending rapidly on a trajectory that was about 1 nautical mile short of the runway
which led to an inadvertent descent below the minimum approach altitude and subsequently into terrain
The airplane struck more trees, a power pole, and power lines before it impacted downsloping terrain in a large gulley north of the runway 18 threshold.

chain.label: both flight crewmembers fatally injured
chain.trigger: The captain and first officer were fatally injured, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for both flight crewmembers was blunt force injuries
